bare noun phrases, no verbs, no articles. Head noun is a text-type again (abstract, preprint), never a topic. [length/density] [register] [domain] TEXT-TYPE + 'in ___ style' + [', -ing clause' | 'with ___' | 'focused on <broad subject>']

bare noun phrases, queries asking for short Greek mythology passages, but specified by style and format rather than by content. Template : [length] + [register adj] + [domain adj] + HEAD NOUN + 'in a ___ style/tone/register' + [', -ing clause' | 'with ___']

bare noun phrases headed by a text-type (entry, note, explanation, prose), usually front-loaded with length and reference/linguistic modifiers. Template: [length] [dictionary/encyclopedic/technical/linguistic] TEXT-TYPE + ['with' examples/glosses/notation] + ['in a ___ style/tone/register'] + [', defining/explaining/comparing ___']; articles and finite verbs are rare.

mostly bare noun phrases headed by comment, note, discussion, explanation, or text, with 'informal', 'conversational', and 'explanatory' repeatedly stacked before the head. Template: [length] informal [domain] TEXT-TYPE + 'with' [hedges/asides/examples] + [tone/style phrase or 'like a forum/blog/Q&A'] + [', discussing/clarifying/analyzing ___']; occasional prompts instead use 'text containing/with the phrase ___'.

bare noun phrases headed by prose, narrative, writing, exposition, entry, or passage; modifiers nearly always stack formal/factual/encyclopedic with historical/biographical. Template: [length/density] [formal/factual] [historical/biographical/encyclopedic] TEXT-TYPE + 'in/with' [tone/style/detail] + [', summarizing/presenting/explaining ___']; no direct questions or hard lexical constraints.

bare noun phrases headed by prose, writing, entry, text, summary, or explanation; high repetition of encyclopedic/reference/factual/neutral modifiers and comma-separated adjective chains. Template: [length/density] encyclopedic [domain] TEXT-TYPE + 'in/with' [formal/objective/informational tone] + ['like a reference article/entry'] + [', defining/describing/summarizing ___'].

elliptical noun-phrase constraints built around the literal heads 'text' or 'sentence'. Template: [length] text/sentence + 'containing/with/talking about/saying/describing' + [exact or approximate count | quoted required token | positional condition | topic/fact]; positional phrases include 'in the middle' and 'finishing by', while style and tone modifiers are mostly absent.

formulaic answer-seeking noun phrases. Dominant templates: '[short] text containing the answer for : <wh-question>' and '[short] text answering directly or indirectly the question : <question>'; the embedded questions follow a spaced colon and are often lowercase. A smaller tail uses 'text that starts/finishes ___' or 'text where ___' structural constraints.

relative-clause or participial constraint prompts headed by 'text', not style descriptions. Dominant templates: 'text beginning with <quote/statement/attribution>' and 'text where <quotation> is followed by <attribution>'; ordered components are chained with 'then', 'followed by', 'before', and 'later', often ending in another quote or aside.

document-structure prompts headed by 'text' or 'passage', followed by 'beginning/opening with', 'organized/structured as', 'signed with', or a 'where/that' relative clause. They enumerate ordered blocks such as headings, datelines, lists, tables, prose, and signatures, using repeated 'then', 'and', and 'ends with' transitions rather than tone adjectives.

mostly long structural prompts headed by 'text' and a relative or participial clause: 'text where ___', 'text that opens/begins with ___', or 'text beginning with ___'. Each chains stages with 'then', 'turns/shifts to', 'returns to', and 'ends/closes with', typically moving from an announcement or setup through details to an invitation or call to action; only the first two use compact style-label noun phrases.

mostly bare noun phrases headed by a text type such as abstract, paper, passage, or prose; stacked length, register, and scientific-domain modifiers are followed by in-style, with, focused-on, or participial clauses
queries about promotional commercial content, template : [text type] in a [style label] style, [tone adjectives], with/focused on optional:[broad  elements]

a mix of short text-about, text-mentioning, and text-containing noun phrases and longer bare noun phrases headed by note, reference, prose, summary, or writing, with mythology as the domain and trailing style, tone, citation, or purpose modifiers

mostly article-less noun phrases headed by prose, narrative, exposition, entry, or writing, with stacked encyclopedic, historical, factual, and formal modifiers followed by in, with, and participial clauses

bare noun-phrase prompts headed by commentary, discussion, explanation, note, reply, or definition, heavily modified by informal, conversational, and explanatory labels plus chained with, like, about, and participial phrases

bare noun phrases headed by news report, brief, paragraph, article, or interview, with journalistic modifiers and trailing in or with phrases that enumerate tone, quotations, density, audience, and purpose

formulaic bare noun phrases headed by AP-style report, brief, wire, list, or article; optional concise or subject modifiers precede the head, while with phrases list tone, inverted-pyramid structure, quotations, attribution, or other features

very short lower-case noun phrases headed by text, with an optional article or length modifier and one simple postmodifier: about, talking about, containing, or a that-clause expressing inclusion or exclusion

formulaic lower-case noun phrases headed by text or sentence, usually using containing followed by a numeric length or quoted token, with variants using with, finishing by, saying, or that has and comparators such as exactly, around, more than, less than, or between

five bare noun phrases headed by note, explanation, or writing, built from stacked dictionary, reference, technical, and instructional modifiers plus about, of, with, or using phrases and comma-separated tone and feature lists

bare noun phrases headed by entry, note, writing, text, or explanation, typically following the template concise plus dictionary-style, glossary-style, or encyclopedic modifiers, then with clauses or defining and explaining participles

article-less noun phrases headed by prose, writing, text, entry, or list, with repeated encyclopedic, factual, neutral, and formal modifiers followed by with or like clauses and explaining, describing, presenting, or summarizing participles

lower-case text noun phrases: the first group repeats short text containing the answer for or text answering directly or indirectly the question followed by a colon and wh-question; the rest use starts, begins, opens, or finishes clauses to impose exact question-and-answer ordering

relational noun-phrase prompts beginning text beginning with or text where and specifying a rigid left-to-right sequence with then, followed by, later, and ending with; the slots name quotations, blanks, parentheses, symbols, corrections, replacements, and examples

uniform text where or text that begins relational prompts encoding an ordered sequence with then, and then, followed by, resumes, returns, or closes; each sequence starts from an announcement or change and explicitly tracks intervening turns

mostly text that begins or opens prompts specifying a multi-step sequence with then, shifts to, and ends or closes with; recurring structural slots include announcements, headings, lists, invitations, benefit claims, and calls to action

noun phrases headed by text, passage, or analysis and modified by relative clauses or with phrases; most use begins or opens, then, adds, and pivots to describe two- or three-step sequences marked by tentative, cautious, speculative, and qualifying language
all queries are almost like this : 'Text that quotes someone and says who said it.'

noun-phrase prompts headed by text, passage, or entries and modified by that, where, beginning, or ending clauses; many follow begins or opens with a heading or list, then prose or another list, and ends with a final enumeration
These describe the envelope around a text rather than anything inside a sentence: datelines, headlines, timestamps, usernames etc..

lower-case relational prompts beginning text that opens, starts, or defines, or text where; they encode a mostly three-part rhetorical sequence linked by then, finally, and closes with, using abstract slots such as claim, correction, qualification, contrast, and example

mostly lower-case text where prompts that encode three- or four-step discourse skeletons with then, contrast, qualification, correction, exception, concession, reversal, and return; a few shorter variants are headed by passage or writing or specify literal cues such as although and but
queries about text size/length
[AP-style news] with [tone description] , [small comment about the structure] and [additional stylistic features].
adjective-dense noun-phrase queries naming an academic abstract or journal style, followed by technical-domain, tone, density, and explanatory-purpose modifiers

queries beginning with 'text where' or 'text that', then specifying a sequential rhetorical template through chained 'then' clauses involving claims, qualifications, corrections, contrasts, concessions, examples, and exceptions
all queries are almost like this : 'Text beginning with a quote then an attribution tag'
modifier-heavy noun-phrase queries naming an encyclopedic, dictionary, or reference-entry style, followed by factuality, tone, formality, density, subject-area, and explanatory-purpose constraints
[Genre or text type] with [tone/style], [structural or linguistic features], and [a focus on explaining language usage].
